blocks.html:
A hub-to-hub link is a thin layer on top of two working hub domains. Bring each domain up with the single-hub guide, then add the inter-hub link. We have not demoed this, so treat the order below as the intended sequence to validate.

Order of operations

1. Per domain     stand up HUB A + its servers, and HUB B + its servers,
                  each via the single-hub IaC guide (certs, /ca_public trust,
                  Keycloak tak_ groups, templated configs + policy)
2. Shared groups  ensure the shared taxonomy (tak_SHARED_COP, …) exists in every
                  deployment's Keycloak across both domains
3. Cross-trust    fan HUB A CA → HUB B fed-truststore, and HUB B CA → HUB A fed-truststore
4. Inter-hub link add to each hub's policy: peer-hub CA Group + (one side) an Outgoing
                  node to peer:9102 + edges filtered to Allowed Groups = SHARED_COP;
                  re-apply both policies
5. Connect        the initiating hub connects to peer:9102 → mTLS succeeds → both policies admit
6. Verify         assert the inter-hub link + selective cross-domain flow (below)

Steps 1 and 2 are the prerequisite domains; 3 and 4 are the only new IaC; 5 is automatic.

Verify without clicking

  • Inter-hub link up. On each hub's Active Connections, the peer appears (one side as a hub-server, the other as a hub-client). Script the check via the policy-manager endpoint behind the UI.
  • Shared data crosses domains. Inject a SHARED_COP-tagged event on a server under HUB A and assert it reaches a server under HUB B, and back. Use a probe client or the Marti API.
  • Local data does not cross. Inject a *_LOCAL event in domain A and assert it never appears in domain B, which proves the inter-hub filter holds at the boundary.

Gate the pipeline on all three.

Idempotent reconcile

The inter-hub link is derived state too:

  • Add a hub: cross-trust its CA with the central hub, add a peer-hub CA Group plus a filtered edge to the central hub's policy, and re-apply. The new domain joins.
  • Change what is shared: edit the allowed/disallowed groups on the inter-hub edges and re-apply on both hubs.
  • Rotate a hub CA: re-issue via RASENMAEHER, re-fan the new PEM to the peer's truststore, and re-apply.

→ Next: Scaling to many groups.
